What it grades is the other half of the line: when the agent names what would advance the tier, it must name research-plan and never question-selection, because advancing a tier is a search on the question already answered rather than a new question. judge_context: This scenario has ONE open question and no conflicts. At `probable` the agent resolves it (§7) and completes the project (§8), so the next-step line correctly says the project is complete. Do not charge that.

What this test is about is the OTHER half of the line: when the agent names what would advance the tier, it must route that to **research-plan**. Naming **question-selection** is the failure this test exists for — advancing a tier is a SEARCH on the question already answered, not a new question. This is the routing section E changed.
Naming BOTH research-plan and question-selection is not a pass: the point of the change is that one of them is wrong, so offering both leaves the caller to pick.
Naming a record that would advance the tier is required, and it must be a reasonably obtainable one. A privacy-restricted or sealed record (a recent vital record under embargo) does not count.
Saying nothing at all about advancing the tier is also a fail: the tier is below `proved` and named searches remain.
Do not charge the agent on the TIER here. That `probable` is correct on this scenario is `ut_proof_conclusion_d7g`'s subject; this test is only about where it routes.
DATES — the 1832/1833 discrepancy is real fixture content, not an internal inconsistency to charge.
